clue.text: Dandy would have this funny football gear

definitions.meaning: The Dandy was a long-running British children's comic full of cartoon stories told in panels
comic means funny and a strip is a footballer's kit

explanation.surface: A fop would wear this amusing football kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dandy' with its capital looks like a dapper man; it is The Dandy, a British children's comic. Read the second half as 'comic' (funny) plus 'strip' (a team's kit).
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon story in panels is what a children's comic paper prints, and a funny kit is a comic strip read word by word.

clue.text: US soldier climbs up in vehicle for a smoke

indicators.note: the soldier is placed inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing up means the soldier's letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: GI is the usual term for an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier clambers into a car to have a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbs up' means read upwards, so the soldier is turned before going into the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled tobacco leaf is something one smokes, so a smoke is a fair name for it.

clue.text: Not very intelligent about women to bury in December?

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for dim-witted is read backwards

parts.note: dim means not very intelligent
to inter is to bury

explanation.surface: A rather stupid man buries women in December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns DIM into MID. The question mark flags that December is an example: the middle of the northern winter.
explanation.definitionFit: December falls in the depth of the cold season in the northern hemisphere, so it is an example of that season's middle.

clue.text: Senior policeman wants "The Hay Wain"?

definitions.meaning: the head of a British county police force holds this title
The Hay Wain is the best-known painting by John Constable, so it is his principal work

explanation.surface: A top police officer covets a famous landscape painting.
explanation.walkthrough: John Constable was an English landscape painter and The Hay Wain is his most famous picture, so it is the 'chief Constable'. In Britain the same title names the head of a police force.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a regional British police force bears this title, and the famous painting is Constable's foremost work.

clue.text: Proposition of article upset Rome

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: upset signals that the letters of the city name are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A proposal from a newspaper piece annoyed the Romans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' is the anagram signal, working on the city name only; the article stays in front unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a proposition is a statement to be proved, which is what this word names.

clue.text: Lettuce which was once fatal for many passengers

definitions.meaning: a crisp round lettuce variety shares the name

definitions.text: which was once fatal for many passengers
definitions.meaning: the Titanic sank in 1912 after striking a floating mass of ice, and many passengers died

explanation.surface: A salad leaf linked to a famous maritime disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp salad variety bears the name of the floating ice mass that sank the Titanic.

clue.text: Ring a friend, it could be of value

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Phoning a friend might prove worthwhile, as on a quiz show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring a friend' reads as making a phone call; the ring is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious stone is something valuable, and this milky gemstone is one.

clue.text: Smooth feathers about to be seen in female swan

indicators.note: the short word for about is placed inside the swan word

parts.note: a female swan is called a pen
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A swan grooming its plumage is nearly in view.
explanation.walkthrough: A female swan is a pen (the male is a cob).
explanation.definitionFit: Birds groom their plumage with their beaks, and that action is this verb.

clue.text: One dead on arrival?

parts.note: late can mean dead, and a comer is one who arrives, so this is someone tardy when arriving

explanation.surface: A grim hospital phrase for a patient who died before reaching casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical phrase 'dead on arrival' misleads; 'late' means both dead and tardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who turns up after the start arrives tardily, and 'late' doubles as a word for deceased.

clue.text: Break out of compound might one say?

definitions.text: Break out of compound might one say?

parts.words: Break out of compound might one say?
parts.note: a bone break that does not pierce the skin is the opposite of a compound break, and a fraction that is not compound is simple

explanation.surface: Sounds like a prisoner escaping from a walled enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break out of compound' suggests a prison escape. In medicine a compound fracture breaks the skin; one that does not is the opposite kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean bone break with unbroken skin is the medical counterpart to a compound one.

clue.text: Divine ornamental gold presented to old US President

indicators.note: ornamental suggests the metal has been worked into a decorative new shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of Dwight Eisenhower, US President in the 1950s

explanation.surface: Decorative gold given to a former American president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ornamental' rearranges GOLD into GODL, followed by IKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resembling a deity in nature can be called divine.

clue.text: Conspicuous source of wealth in hospital department

indicators.note: the source of wealth sits inside the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
a mine is a source of wealth, as in 'a gold mine'

explanation.surface: A hospital ward proves to be a notable money-spinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguished person stands out, so prominent or noticeable fits.

clue.text: Provide more resources and control for church

parts.note: to rein in is to control
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Extra money and tighter management for a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending extra troops or supplies to strengthen something is what this verb describes.

clue.text: Short film features a new scare

indicators.note: features means contains, so the film word holds the other letters

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film

explanation.surface: A short movie includes a fresh fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden fright or alarm is a scare.

clue.text: Get one up in alfresco party

parts.note: alfresco means outdoors, out
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Scoring points over a rival at an outdoor party.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or better someone is to get one up on them.

clue.text: Disliking that woman Margaret's type of clothes?

parts.note: off means having lost a taste for, as in 'off one's food'
that is read as the definite article the
Peg is a pet form of Margaret

explanation.surface: Not keen on Margaret's dress sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Peg is a traditional short form of the name Margaret.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-made garments bought from a rack, not tailored, are described by this phrase.

clue.text: Element of silence surrounds girl meeting one

indicators.note: the silence word goes round the outside of the girl and the one

parts.note: mum means silent, as in 'keep mum'
Agnes is a girl's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Silence falls around a girl on a first date.
explanation.definitionFit: This light silvery metal is a chemical element.

clue.text: Wrote The Last of the Mohicans?

definitions.text: Wrote The Last of the Mohicans?

parts.words: Wrote The Last of the Mohicans?
parts.note: the last of the Mohicans is an Indian, and wrote suggests writing fluid, so the phrase pictures a pen dipped in a dark drawing liquid

explanation.surface: Asks who wrote the famous novel by James Fenimore Cooper.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised title points at the novel; the clue instead pictures a Native American (in the old term) plus the stuff one writes with.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense black drawing liquid bears this name, and the phrase pairs a Mohican with writing fluid.

clue.text: Anticipate trees being attractive to everybody

parts.note: a forest is a mass of trees
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Woodland that appeals to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being attractive to' sits between the pieces as a link, in the sense of trees 'for' everybody; the whole definition is 'Anticipate'.
explanation.definitionFit: To act first and so prevent something is to anticipate it.

clue.text: Church officer used to lacey dressing

indicators.note: dressing suggests the letters are arranged or dressed differently, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A churchwarden is accustomed to lacy vestments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' rearranges TOLACEY.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant who serves at the altar is a minor church officer.

clue.text: Only stairs available? One could get rocket to start?

definitions.meaning: a notice that the lift is off means only the stairs can be used

definitions.text: One could get rocket to start?
definitions.meaning: the moment a rocket leaves the launch pad

explanation.surface: The elevator is broken, so it's stairs or a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch is a rocket's start, and 'lift off' read as two words means the elevator is out of service.

clue.text: Artist takes day to get a right location found by this

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter needs a day to find the right spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Detection equipment using radio waves fixes the position of aircraft and ships.

clue.text: Fuss over a pair of back-to back houses

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house

indicators.note: the second house is turned to face the first, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A row about terraced houses joined at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair of' gives two HOs; 'back-to back' turns the second, making HOOH, then A follows. Back-to-back houses are a British style of terrace sharing a rear wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A commotion or to-do over something trivial is a fuss.

clue.text: It could produce oil, see, used by Spain

definitions.text: It could produce oil, see, used by Spain

indicators.note: could produce suggests the letters of oil may yield another arrangement

parts.note: v stands for vide, Latin for see
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A tree yielding oil, much used in Spanish cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It could produce' scrambles just the word oil; v is the dictionary abbreviation of Latin vide (see), and E is Spain's international car code.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit of this Mediterranean tree is pressed for oil, and Spain grows it widely.

clue.text: Serve away from here in Paris at a theatre that's empty

parts.note: off means away
ici is French for here

indicators.note: an empty theatre keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Performing far from home at an empty Parisian theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's empty' leaves T and E from 'theatre'.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve as referee or to preside over a ceremony is to perform an official role.

clue.text: Chemical always found round street

indicators.note: the word for always is placed round the street abbreviation

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A chemical keeps turning up around the street.
explanation.definitionFit: This organic compound formed from an acid and an alcohol is a chemical.

clue.text: Give money to get, say, Harris pattern

indicators.note: the payment word gets the island word placed within it

parts.note: to pay is to give money
Harris is an island in the Scottish Outer Hebrides, an isle

explanation.surface: Paying for a Harris tweed design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harris pattern' suggests Harris tweed; Harris is an example (say) of an isle, which goes inside PAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A swirling teardrop textile design is known by this name.

clue.text: Old copper's on panel of eye specialist

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a list, such as a panel of names, is a roster

explanation.surface: A retired policeman sits on an eye doctor's board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' means a police officer in the surface but is the metal here.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for an ophthalmologist or optician, a doctor of eyes.

clue.text: Song of single entertainer

indicators.note: of here means made from, so the answer is formed from letters running through the two words

explanation.surface: A tune performed by a solo artiste.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'sinGLE Entertainer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-song for unaccompanied voices is a glee, a traditional English song form.

clue.text: Not an altruist? One can only say "aye"!

definitions.meaning: someone who puts their own interests first is the opposite of an altruist
aye sounds like I, so one forever saying 'I' is chasing their own interests

explanation.surface: A selfish person who only ever agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: "Aye" (yes) sounds like 'I': someone whose only word is 'I' is out for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A person pursuing personal gain above others is an egotist, the opposite of an altruist.
